summary: H.R. 10585, the Civilian Climate Corps for Jobs and Justice Act, amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a Civilian Climate Corps. The program aims to help communities respond to climate change, complete clean energy and conservation projects, and ease the transition to a clean economy while providing education, job training, and career pathways, with a special focus on under-resourced communities.

affected_groups.effect: Receive living allowances of at least $20 per hour, health care, training, supportive services, educational benefits up to $25,000, and collective bargaining rights including the right to strike.
affected_groups.group: Civilian Climate Corps Members and Participants

affected_groups.effect: Receive targeted investments, clean energy infrastructure, disaster mitigation, and environmental remediation, with at least 50 percent of corps labor and investment dedicated to these areas.
States, local subdivisions, territories, Indian tribes, non-profits, labor organizations, and higher education institutions can apply for 100-percent-cost grants to run climate service projects.

key_provisions: Establishes the Civilian Climate Corps under the Corporation for National and Community Service, consisting of a national climate service program and a national climate service grant program.
Sets ambitious position growth targets starting at 75,000 total positions in fiscal year 2027 and scaling up to 600,000 total positions by fiscal year 2031.
Requires that at least 50 percent of corps labor and investment support projects based in under-resourced communities of need, including specific allocations for Indian country.

Provides members with a living allowance equivalent to at least $20 per hour (with adjustments for inflation and prevailing wages for specific labor types), health care benefits, supportive services, and up to $25,000 in educational benefits per term of service.
Establishes labor rights for members, including the right to join a labor organization, collectively bargain, and strike without being permanently replaced.

Provides significant supplemental appropriations totaling billions of dollars across fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for the Civilian Climate Corps and existing national service programs like AmeriCorps and VISTA.
Excludes national service educational awards and student loan repayments under the program from gross income for tax purposes.
missing_information: Exact overall net cost of healthcare benefits, as the text states 'such sums as may be necessary' rather than a fixed dollar amount.
Specific details on how the broader federal budget will offset the multi-billion-dollar authorizations and tax exclusions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10585, the Civilian Climate Corps for Jobs and Justice Act, amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a Civilian Climate Corps. The program aims to help communities respond to climate change, complete clean energy and conservation projects, and ease the transition to a clean economy while providing education, job training, and career pathways, with a special focus on under-resourced communities.
summary_detail.significance: This bill represents a sweeping federal labor mobilization and investment strategy linking national community service directly to climate change mitigation and environmental justice. By creating hundreds of thousands of paid positions, extensive training pipelines, and robust labor protections, the legislation proposes a substantial structural expansion of domestic climate resiliency and workforce development efforts.
